analysis.summary: BHP FY26 delivered a strong beat on underlying metrics versus the prior year, with Underlying attributable profit of US$13.2bn (+30%) and Underlying EBITDA of US$32.9bn (+27%), driven overwhelmingly by a 35% surge in copper realised prices and record WAIO iron ore production. Cash conversion was excellent: US$21.8bn of operating cash flow converted to US$9.8bn of free cash flow (+83%), supported by US$4.3bn from the Antamina silver streaming transaction. The final dividend of US$0.99/share (fully franked, 72% payout ratio) brings total FY26 returns to US$8.7bn, the highest in four years, signalling balance sheet confidence with net debt at just US$8.7bn (0.3x EBITDA). The single biggest forward risk is copper price mean-reversion: copper contributed 54% of Group Underlying EBITDA at a US$5.74/lb realised price, yet FY27 guidance implies a production step-down to 1,650-1,800kt alongside unit cost headwinds from diesel and FX.
analysis.full_analysis:
## Executive summary
- **Copper is now the earnings engine**: for the first time, the Copper segment contributed >50% (54%) of Group Underlying EBITDA at a record US$18.2bn, up 48% on FY25, driven by a 35% increase in average realised copper price to US$5.74/lb.
- **All-round financial strength**: revenue +15% to US$58.8bn, Underlying EBITDA margin expanded 6 percentage points to 59% (highest in four years), ROCE lifted to 26.1% from 20.6%, and free cash flow nearly doubled to US$9.8bn.
- **Balance sheet rapidly deleveraged**: net debt fell from US$12.9bn to US$8.7bn (0.3x Underlying EBITDA), below the US$10-20bn target range, aided by the US$4.3bn Antamina silver streaming transaction.
- **Statutory profit dragged by large exceptional items**: US$2.3bn Jansen impairment and US$1.1bn Samarco provision reduced attributable profit to US$9.8bn (+9%), masking the 30% underlying earnings growth.
- **Red flag — FY27 copper volume guidance implies a step-down**: Group copper guidance of 1,650-1,800kt is materially below FY26 actual of 1,953kt, reflecting planned grade decline at Escondida (feed grade expected ~0.70% vs ~0.90% in FY26) and complexity at Spence.

## Key numbers

| Metric | FY26 | FY25 | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | US$58,760m | US$51,262m | +15% |
| Underlying EBITDA | US$32,947m | US$25,978m | +27% |
| Underlying EBITDA margin | 59% | 53% | +6pp |
| Statutory (attributable) profit | US$9,833m | US$9,019m | +9% |
| Underlying attributable profit | US$13,204m | US$10,157m | +30% |
| Bridge: exceptional items (after tax) | -US$3.4bn | -US$1.1bn | Jansen impairment US$2.3bn + Samarco US$1.1bn |
| Underlying basic EPS | 260.0 US cps | 200.2 US cps | +30% |
| Basic (statutory) EPS | 193.6 US cps | 177.8 US cps | +9% |
| Net operating cash flow | US$21,778m | US$18,692m | +17% |
| Capex & exploration | US$10,257m | US$9,794m | +5% |
| Free cash flow | US$9,800m | US$5,300m | +83% |
| Net debt | US$8,694m | US$12,924m | -33% |
| Gearing ratio | 13.4% | 19.8% | -6.4pp |
| Underlying ROCE | 26.1% | 20.6% | +5.5pp |
| Adjusted effective tax rate | 36.5% | 37.2% | -0.7pp |

## Quality of earnings
- **Cash conversion is high**: US$21.8bn operating cash flow against US$32.9bn Underlying EBITDA implies ~66% EBITDA-to-OCF conversion, which is normal for a capital-intensive miner paying substantial taxes (US$12.4bn to governments) and Samarco obligations (US$2.0bn). Free cash flow of US$9.8bn after US$10.3bn capex is genuinely impressive.
- **Non-recurring boosts to net debt reduction**: the Antamina silver streaming proceeds (US$4.3bn) and asset sales (US$0.8bn) flatter the balance sheet improvement. Underlying free cash flow was ~US$9.8bn before these — still strong, but the silver streaming proceeds are a one-time event.
- **Exceptional items are substantial and not trivial to dismiss**: the US$2.3bn Jansen impairment (reflecting JS2 cost blowout from US$4.9bn to US$6.9bn) and US$1.1bn Samarco charge are lumpy but not purely non-cash — Samarco cash outflows were US$2.0bn in FY26 with ~US$1.4bn expected in FY27-28 combined. Management's emphasis on underlying figures is understandable but the impairment signals real capital allocation miscalculation at Jansen.
- **Unit cost discipline creditable**: group unit costs fell 6.1% on a copper equivalent production weighted basis despite 4% Australian inflation, 3.7% Chilean inflation, and a ~30% increase in diesel prices. Escondida unit costs fell 10% to US$1.07/lb; Copper SA fell 73% to US$0.32/lb (materially aided by gold/silver/uranium by-product credits at elevated prices — this will be price-sensitive).
- **Working capital/inventory**: the EBITDA waterfall discloses net favourable inventory movements of US$1.1bn in operating cash costs — primarily timing of shipments at Escondida and Spence, not structural. This could reverse in FY27 given the volume step-down.
- **DSO/receivables**: not separately disclosed in the results release; no unusual flag.

## Management framing
**Rating: Promotional — but not misleading**
- The presentation leads emphatically with the copper theme and 54% EBITDA contribution — legitimately a milestone, but the deck buries the fact that Group copper production actually fell 3% year-on-year (1,953kt vs 2,017kt in FY25) and FY27 guidance is 1,650-1,800kt, a further step down of up to 15%.
- The Jansen impairment is disclosed but framed as 'world class asset at the low end of the cost curve when fully ramped up.' The cost estimate for JS2 has blown out 41% (US$4.9bn to US$6.9bn) and the IRR rationale for the project has demonstrably deteriorated — management acknowledge this only obliquely.
- The silver streaming transaction (US$4.3bn) is highlighted as 'unlocking undervalued capital' — a legitimate monetisation, but it permanently transfers silver economics at Antamina to a third party. The presentation does not quantify the ongoing cost (i.e., the value of silver stream surrendered).
- The BOS/technology savings claims (US$5.1bn in initial year savings since FY20) are internally validated, not externally audited, and 'initial year' savings may double-count with ongoing productivity — caveat applies.
- WAIO C1 unit cost methodology was restated in FY26 to include inventory movements, making the headline increase to US$19.66/t appear more benign than the US$18.72/t that would have applied under the old methodology. BHP discloses this, but it requires close reading.
- Management withholds explicit FY26 vs consensus commentary and provides no EPS guidance for FY27.

## Segments

| Segment | FY26 Revenue | FY26 Underlying EBITDA | Margin | Change in EBITDA |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Copper (statutory) | US$29,031m | US$18,187m | 70% | +48% |
| — Escondida | US$17,054m | US$12,440m | ~73% | +45% |
| — Copper SA | US$6,011m | US$3,203m | ~53% | +65% |
| — Pampa Norte | US$2,857m | US$1,560m | ~55% | +23% |
| Iron Ore (statutory) | US$23,883m | US$14,529m | 61% | +1% |
| — WAIO | US$23,726m | US$14,667m | 62% | +2% |
| Coal (statutory) | US$5,590m | US$832m | 15% (BMA 18%) | +45% |
| — BMA | US$3,876m | US$702m | 18% | +19% |
| — NSWEC | US$1,851m | US$342m | 18% | +48% |
| Group & Unallocated (inc. Potash) | US$256m | -US$601m | n/m | loss increased |

**Key observations**:
- Iron ore Underlying EBITDA was virtually flat (+1%) despite record volumes — higher realised prices (+3%) offset a stronger AUD and diesel cost inflation. WAIO unit costs rose 6% to US$19.66/t; FY27 guidance of US$20.25-21.75/t signals further pressure.
- Coal recovered sharply: BMA steelmaking coal price +8% and NSWEC benefited from lower strip ratio mine sequencing (cash harvest before FY30 closure). Coal is now structurally diminishing and management is explicit about it.
- Potash (Jansen) absorbed US$1.8bn capex in FY26, producing zero revenue, while generating the US$2.3bn impairment. JS2 cost estimate blowout to US$6.9bn is the most significant negative financial disclosure in this result.

## Balance sheet
- Net debt fell from US$12.9bn to US$8.7bn, now below the US$10-20bn target range, with gearing at 13.4%.
- Key drivers: US$9.8bn free cash flow + US$4.3bn Antamina silver streaming + US$0.8bn asset sales, offset by US$6.8bn dividends to shareholders, US$2.4bn to non-controlling interests, and US$2.0bn Samarco payments.
- The GIP WAIO inland power transaction (US$2.0bn received in August 2026 for 49% stake in a power partnership) provides additional liquidity but introduces a partner into the Pilbara infrastructure ecosystem.
- Debt maturity profile is well-laddered: predominantly capital markets (89%), mix of USD, EUR, and GBP bonds with no material near-term cliff. Moody's A1 stable / Fitch A stable — no change.
- Samarco provision: US$5.2bn remains on balance sheet (down from US$5.8bn); future cash obligations of ~US$0.9bn in FY27 and ~US$0.5bn in FY28 (BHP share). UK group action remains unresolved with second stage trial scheduled April 2027 to March 2028 — a material contingent liability.
- Pro-forma for the final dividend (US$5.0bn), net debt would rise to ~US$13.7bn, back within the target range. The balance sheet strength therefore partly reflects the timing of the dividend — it is not structurally under-leveraged.

## Dividend and capital allocation
- Final dividend: US$0.99/share (fully franked), 72% payout ratio on underlying earnings.
- Total FY26 dividends: US$1.72/share (172 US cps), up 56% vs FY25 110 cps. This is the highest total annual dividend since FY22.
- Minimum 50% payout ratio policy maintained; the 72% payout reflects balance sheet headroom and strong FCF, but is not a new sustainable floor.
- Capex rising: FY27 guidance ~US$11bn, expected to remain ~US$11bn in FY28 and on average FY29-31. Growth capex ~US$3.8bn in FY27, predominantly copper-focused (US$5.4bn of FY27 total capex allocated to Copper). Capital intensity is increasing as Jansen Stage 2 (US$6.9bn) and Escondida New Concentrator (US$5.4-6.3bn) consume capital simultaneously from ~CY28.
- No share buyback announced for FY26 — consistent with preference for growth capex over buybacks.
- The US$10bn 'unlocking undervalued capital' aspiration is explicitly not a commitment — US$6.3bn is agreed (silver streaming + GIP), with up to US$3.7bn still aspirational.

## Guidance and outlook
- **Copper production FY27**: 1,650-1,800kt — a material step-down from 1,953kt in FY26. Escondida grade decline (to ~0.70% from ~0.90%) is the primary driver.
- **WAIO FY27**: 253-264Mt (286-298Mt 100% basis); unit cost US$20.25-21.75/t — costs rising on diesel and AUD headwinds.
- **BMA FY27**: 18.5-20.5Mt (37-41Mt 100% basis); unit cost US$126-137/t.
- **Capex FY27**: ~US$11bn (unchanged); FY28 also ~US$11bn (previously lower), reflecting Jansen Stage 2 escalation.
- **Tax rate FY27**: 35-40% adjusted effective tax rate.
- **No revenue or earnings guidance provided** — standard for BHP.
- **Jansen Stage 1**: on track for mid-CY27 first production. JS2 delayed to late-FY31 with cost now US$6.9bn.
- **Escondida New Concentrator**: FID targeted CY27-28, first production CY31-32; project economics improved (IRR 16-18% vs prior 13-16%) but capex range widened to US$5.4-6.3bn.
- **Vicuña Stage I FID**: potential as early as end of CY26 (non-operated JV).

## Positives
- **Record copper earnings**: Copper segment Underlying EBITDA of US$18.2bn at 70% margin is exceptional; Escondida unit costs at US$1.07/lb (lowest in years) and Copper SA at US$0.32/lb are genuinely world-class.
- **Record WAIO production and shipments** for seven consecutive years as lowest-cost major iron ore producer globally; C1 cost US$16.40/t, approximately US$10/t below closest peer.
- **Free cash flow of US$9.8bn** (+83%) demonstrates the portfolio's earnings quality; copper growth is self-funded (Copper segment generated US$6.9bn FCF in FY26).
- **Balance sheet at 0.3x EBITDA** provides maximum strategic optionality and supports the generous dividend.
- **By-product windfall**: US$4.5bn of by-product revenue from copper assets (+45%); gold at US$4,300/oz, silver at elevated prices — a structural advantage of the Copper SA and Escondida asset mix.
- **ROCE of 26.1%**: Escondida at 53% and WAIO at 41% are genuinely elite returns on large capital bases.
- **Project pipeline optionality**: Resolution (1.86Bt at 1.52% Cu declared as Mineral Resource for first time), Vicuña, Cerro Colorado restart — all at various stages, providing a long runway.

## Negatives / red flags
- **Copper production step-down in FY27**: FY27 guidance midpoint of 1,725kt is ~11% below FY26 actuals; Escondida grade decline (0.70% feed grade) is not short-lived — medium-term guidance (FY28-31) is 900-1,000ktpa at Escondida, below FY26's 1,261kt.
- **Jansen cost blowout**: JS2 estimate up 41% to US$6.9bn, triggering a US$2.3bn impairment. The combined JS1+JS2 investment is now ~US$15.3bn for a project that will not be fully ramped until the early 2030s. At long-term consensus potash prices, returns are thin.
- **Rising capex trajectory**: US$11bn in FY27 and FY28 constrains dividend upside and leaves less room for buybacks; if copper prices soften, free cash flow could compress sharply while growth spending continues.
- **Samarco tail risk**: US$5.2bn provision, UK group action second stage trial not until April 2027-March 2028 — the contingent liability upside is unbounded; BHP has already been found liable under Brazilian law by the UK High Court.
- **WAIO unit cost pressure**: FY27 guidance midpoint of ~US$21/t represents a ~7% increase on FY26's US$19.66/t, driven by diesel, AUD, and CD4 renewal. Sustaining cost of ~US$7/t per tonne is rising as the asset ages.
- **Copper SA unit cost flatters via by-products**: FY26's US$0.32/lb net unit cost is calculated after gold (US$4,300+/oz), silver, and uranium credits. If gold prices normalise, net unit costs could triple, making the FY27 guidance range of US$0.30-0.80/lb look like a wide uncertainty band.
- **Coal is a shrinking but non-trivial distraction**: NSWEC exits by FY30, BMA subject to Queensland royalty headwinds limiting further investment — coal contributed only 3% of Group EBITDA at a 15% margin. The distraction cost is manageable but the rehabilitation/closure provision is a drag.
- **Fatality at BMA post-period**: a contractor fatality at Peak Downs in July 2026 (FY27) is a social and operational risk. Investigations ongoing; potential for operational restrictions.

## Bottom line
**Bull case**: Copper remains structurally tight (demand growth from data centres, electrification, grid investment; supply constrained by grade decline and project underinvestment). BHP is the world's largest copper producer at the world's lowest cost. Escondida's New Concentrator (FID CY27-28, first production CY31-32) and Copper SA Phase 1 expansion (~500ktpa Cu by 2035) add meaningful volume at competitive capital intensity. At spot copper prices (~US$6.60/lb per BHP's scenario analysis), cumulative 5-year free cash flow could reach ~US$50bn — implying the stock is cheap on a through-cycle basis. The 3-4% CuEq production CAGR to FY35 is credible given BHP's track record of meeting guidance.

**Bear case**: The FY26 result was heavily dependent on a copper price that averaged US$5.74/lb — consensus long-term is US$4.76/lb (UBS). A reversion to consensus reduces Copper EBITDA by roughly US$4bn and Group EBITDA by ~12-15%. Simultaneously, capex is rising to US$11bn+ annually, WAIO unit costs are heading above US$21/t, and Jansen is consuming US$2bn/year for a potash project with questionable returns and a history of cost overruns. Net debt could rebound to US$15bn+ within two years at consensus prices while still paying 50%+ dividends and funding growth.

**What would change the view**: (1) a sustained copper price above US$5.50/lb justifies the current growth pipeline at premium returns; (2) successful Vicuña Stage I FID with credible cost estimates would de-risk the mid-2030s production target; (3) any further Jansen cost escalation beyond US$6.9bn for JS2 would be a material negative; (4) resolution of the UK Samarco group action in BHP's favour would remove a multi-billion contingent liability overhang.

analysis.summary: FY26 was a year of managed decline, consistent with CSL's own May 2026 pre-announcement, so there was no surprise versus guidance. The underlying NPAT miss versus prior year (-3% reported, -3% at constant currency) was driven by albumin price collapse in China (-17%), iron generic competition crushing CSL Vifor (-16% iron revenue), and a non-recurring avian influenza contract that boosted Seqirus in FY25. Cash conversion remained robust with US$3.5b operating cash flow essentially matching underlying earnings quality, but the statutory result was a US$2.6b net loss after US$7.1b in pre-tax impairments, the majority against CSL Vifor assets. The dividend was held flat at US$2.92 per share, signalling balance sheet confidence but no growth ambition, accompanied by an A$1b buyback completed in FY26 and A$1.1b flagged for FY27. The single biggest forward risk is CSL Vifor's guided ~25% revenue decline in FY27 as TDAPA expires for Velphoro, TAVNEOS loses its marketing authorisation, and iron generics continue to erode the franchise that cost ~$12b to acquire.
analysis.full_analysis:
## Executive Summary
- FY26 was a self-described 'reset year': underlying NPAT fell 3% to US$2,837m and revenue slipped 1% to US$15,797m, both in line with May 2026 guidance, so no earnings surprise.
- The statutory loss of US$2,579m (vs US$3,002m profit in FY25) reflects US$7.1b in pre-tax impairments, overwhelmingly concentrated in CSL Vifor intangibles and goodwill (US$4.9b), plus US$2.1b in other assets (Lengnau PPE, sa-mRNA IP). These are largely non-cash but confirm that the 2022 Vifor acquisition has destroyed substantial value.
- Red flag: FY27 guidance for CSL Vifor revenue to fall ~25% means the segment that cost billions will contribute materially less; combined with anticipated further FY27 impairments of ~US$200m, the Vifor chapter remains painful.
- Bright spots: ANDEMBRY (HAE) launch exceeded expectations with 14% therapy-group growth; HEMGENIX up 25%; Seqirus seasonal influenza up 4% in core; transformation program delivered US$176m cost savings above target, tracking to US$400m by FY27.
- Interim CEO appointment mid-year signals prior strategic direction was inadequate; permanent CEO search is an unresolved governance overhang.

## Key Numbers

| Metric | FY26 | FY25 | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Total Revenue | US$15,797m | US$15,558m | +2% reported / -1% CC |
| Gross Profit (underlying) | US$8,454m | US$8,443m | flat |
| Gross Margin (underlying) | 53.5% | 54.3% | -80bps |
| Operating Result (underlying) | US$6,763m | US$6,827m | -1% |
| R&D (underlying) | US$1,223m | US$1,359m | -10% |
| G&A (underlying) | US$920m | US$1,000m | -8% |
| NPATA (underlying, to CSL shareholders) | US$3,098m | US$3,219m | -4% |
| Underlying NPAT (to CSL shareholders) | US$2,837m | US$2,972m | -5% reported; -3% CC |
| Statutory NPAT (Loss) | -US$2,579m | +US$3,002m | n/m |
| Underlying NPATA EPS | US$6.43 | US$6.65 | -3% |
| Operating Cash Flow | US$3,512m | US$3,561m | -1% |
| Capex | US$766m | ~US$700m est. | +~10% |
| Free Cash Flow (approx.) | ~US$2,746m | ~US$2,861m | ~-4% |
| Net Debt/EBITDA | 1.8x | 1.8x | flat |
| Underlying ETR | 20.8% | 15.9% | +490bps |

## Quality of Earnings
- Operating cash flow of US$3,512m versus underlying NPAT of US$2,837m implies a cash conversion ratio of ~124%, which is healthy and reflects the non-cash amortisation and D&A burden.
- The tax rate jump from 15.9% to 20.8% (management attributes FY25 benefit to FX) reduced underlying NPAT by an estimated ~US$150m; this headwind should partially normalise in FY27.
- R&D spend fell US$136m (-10%) and G&A fell US$80m (-8%), the primary source of the US$176m cost saves; these are genuine P&L improvements but represent partially funded restructuring (US$799m one-off pre-tax restructuring costs in FY26).
- The US$7.1b impairment charge is non-cash but confirms overpayment for Vifor. The pre-tax breakdown: US$4.9b in CSL Vifor intangibles/goodwill, US$0.9b Lengnau PPE, US$0.59b sa-mRNA IP (Arcturus collaboration ended), US$0.5b other PPE. After tax and NCI, the net charge attributable to CSL shareholders is US$4,808m.
- Restructuring cash costs: US$339m paid in FY26, ~US$300m still to be paid in FY27 - a real cash drag on free cash flow not visible in underlying metrics.
- Capex of US$766m (4.9% of revenue) is at multi-year lows; FY27 guided at ~US$1b, so FCF will compress even as operating cash flow holds.

## Management Framing
**Rating: Mixed / Promotional**
- Management consistently leads with constant currency figures (-1% revenue, -3% NPAT) rather than reported figures (+2% revenue but statutory loss), which is technically defensible but optimistic.
- The 'reset year' framing is used to pre-empt criticism of the Vifor impairments, but the US$7.1b write-down acknowledges an acquisition that destroyed significant shareholder value. The word 'impairment' appears in small font relative to the transformation narrative.
- The deck prominently features ANDEMBRY and HEMGENIX growth without proportionate disclosure of albumin (-17%) or iron (-16%) drags at the top-level summary slide.
- The transformation cost-save chart shows escalating bars to FY28, but the reinvestment ratio (~50% of saves to be reinvested in FY27) means net benefit is modest.
- Positive: management does disclose the full impairment bridge in Appendix C with pre-tax, tax, NCI and net-to-CSL columns - this is transparent and appreciated.
- The CEO transition to an interim is briefly mentioned but not discussed in detail; there is no timeline for permanent appointment.

## Segments

| Segment | FY26 Revenue | Change (CC) | Operating Result | Op Margin | Change (bps) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| CSL Behring | US$11,387m | -1% | US$4,612m | 40.5% | -140bps |
| CSL Vifor | US$2,379m | +3% | US$1,252m | 52.6% | +370bps |
| CSL Seqirus | US$2,031m | -8% | US$899m | 44.3% | -230bps |

- **CSL Behring**: Ig flat (Medicare Part D headwind, channel inventory reset), albumin down 17% (China government cost containment), HAE up 14% (ANDEMBRY launch), haemophilia down 1% (legacy FVIII offset by HEMGENIX +25%). GP margin down 70bps to 49.6%. Sales & marketing up 8% (field force investment). This remains the franchise engine but is operating below its historical margin trajectory.
- **CSL Vifor**: Revenue up 3% at CC but this masked by mix. Nephrology dialysis +18% (TDAPA for Velphoro) - this is a one-time regulatory uplift that expires 31 Dec 2026. Iron down 16% from generic competition. TAVNEOS marketing authorisation revoked mid-year. Operating margin expanded 370bps to 52.6% on cost reallocations to Behring, not organic improvement. FY27 guided revenue decline ~25% - this segment is in structural decline.
- **CSL Seqirus**: Revenue down 8% at CC; core seasonal influenza +4% (Fluad +5%, Flucelvax +5%) but masked by -47% in-licensing/other (avian flu non-recurring in FY25) and -1% pandemic fees. Operating margin compressed 230bps to 44.3%. The differentiation strategy (FLUAD, FLUCELVAX RWE) is working in ex-US markets; sa-mRNA collaboration with Arcturus terminated.

## Balance Sheet
- Net debt/EBITDA stable at 1.8x (within 1.5x-2.0x target range), having de-levered from 2.7x in FY23.
- FY27 capex guided at ~US$1b (+$234m vs FY26), driven by Kankakee Ig facility investment, which will compress FCF.
- ~US$300m restructuring cash payments still to flow in FY27.
- A$1b buyback completed FY26; A$1.1b authorised for FY27 - this is shareholder-friendly but should be viewed against elevated capex and restructuring cash commitments.
- Anticipated FY27 impairments ~US$200m (pre-tax) - modest relative to FY26 but confirms the balance sheet clean-up is not complete.
- No covenant disclosures in the presentation; leverage within stated target range provides headroom.

## Dividend and Capital Allocation
- DPS maintained at US$2.92 per share (flat vs FY25), signalling confidence in cash generation despite the statutory loss.
- Buyback of A$1b in FY26 and A$1.1b in FY27 is a meaningful return to shareholders and partially offsets dilution from share-based compensation.
- Capex stepping up to ~US$1b in FY27 represents the Kankakee Ig capacity investment - this is a long-duration bet on Ig demand growth that is strategically sound but capital-intensive.
- The combination of maintained dividend + elevated capex + buyback + restructuring cash outflows (~US$300m) means free cash flow will be under pressure in FY27 despite strong operating cash flow.

## Guidance and Outlook
- **FY27 revenue**: In line with FY26 at constant currency (i.e. flat in real terms).
- **FY27 underlying NPAT**: ~5% growth at constant currency.
- **FY27 FX**: Estimated ~US$50m headwind at current rates.
- **CSL Behring**: Mid-single digit revenue growth; Ig mid-to-high single digit; modest gross margin improvement.
- **CSL Vifor**: Revenue decline ~25% (TDAPA expiry, TAVNEOS loss, iron generics).
- **CSL Seqirus**: Low single digit revenue growth.
- **Capex**: ~US$1b +/- US$100m.
- **Anticipated FY27 impairments**: ~US$200m.
- The ~5% underlying NPAT growth guidance at constant currency is achievable if cost savings of ~US$224m incremental (FY26 to FY27 on the savings ladder) flow through and the ETR normalises, but it requires Behring to execute and Vifor not to deteriorate beyond guided.
- Guidance is more specific than typical CSL historical practice, which is a positive transparency signal.

## Positives
- ANDEMBRY (HAE) launched in 19 markets with HAE therapy revenue up 14% to US$884m - a genuine new growth vector.
- HEMGENIX gene therapy up 25% to US$118m - early but validates the gene therapy platform.
- Cost transformation delivered US$176m in FY26 savings above internal target, tracking to US$400m by FY27.
- Operating cash flow remains robust at US$3.5b with healthy cash conversion vs underlying NPAT.
- Balance sheet deleveraged to 1.8x ND/EBITDA, within target; sufficient capacity for growth optionality.
- Seqirus seasonal influenza core +4% with market share gains in US IDN, Germany first season, France entry; differentiation strategy working.
- Clazakizumab licensed to Eli Lilly for US$100m upfront for non-ESKD indications, recycling pipeline value.
- Net Debt/EBITDA held flat despite US$339m restructuring cash outflows and A$1b buyback in the year.

## Negatives / Red Flags
- US$7.1b pre-tax impairment (net US$4.8b to CSL shareholders) is the largest single write-down in CSL's history and represents an explicit admission that the ~US$12b Vifor acquisition was significantly overvalued.
- CSL Vifor guided to decline ~25% in FY27; the franchise is structurally impaired by generics (iron) and regulatory events (TAVNEOS revoked, TDAPA expiry).
- Albumin revenue down 17% to US$1,115m; China government cost containment is structural, not cyclical, and management's own framing of 'price declining at a slower rate' does not inspire confidence.
- Tax rate jumped from 15.9% to 20.8% (+490bps), absorbing ~US$150m of potential NPAT; the FY25 FX tax benefit does not recur but the higher underlying rate may persist.
- No permanent CEO in place; interim leadership creates strategic uncertainty at a critical transformation juncture.
- Capex rising to ~US$1b in FY27 (+30%) just as operating headwinds intensify, compressing FCF.
- ~US$300m of restructuring cash costs still to be paid in FY27 - a hidden drag on reported FCF not captured in underlying metrics.
- Sa-mRNA collaboration with Arcturus terminated, writing off the associated IP (US$590m pre-tax impairment); this closes a potential mRNA platform optionality.
- R&D spend declined US$136m (-10%); while this is the cost savings program working, sustained R&D cuts risk future pipeline depth.

## Bottom Line
**Bull case**: The transformation program delivers US$400m in run-rate savings by FY27 with ~50% reinvested, Ig demand sustains mid-to-high single digit growth underpinned by robust underlying demand, ANDEMBRY accelerates into a US$1b+ product, and Seqirus consolidates European market share gains. With ETR normalisation and buybacks reducing the share count, FY27 underlying NPAT growth of ~5% at CC is achievable and FY28 could see a step-change as Kankakee capacity comes online and Vifor headwinds lap. At that point CSL would be back to its historical compounding growth mode.

**Bear case**: Vifor deteriorates faster than the guided -25%, China albumin pricing continues to compress (Behring GP margin already at 49.6% and falling), and the cost savings are more than offset by reinvestment and rising capex. The interim CEO search drags, strategic direction stalls, and the market re-rates CSL from a quality compounder to a restructuring story. FX headwinds further erode reported USD earnings for Australian-dollar investors.

**What would change the view**: A permanent CEO appointment with a credible multi-year strategy; evidence in 1H27 that Ig volume growth is reaccelerating above the Medicare Part D drag; CSL Vifor iron stabilisation sooner than expected (biosimilar INJECTAFER competition is the key variable); and FY27 underlying NPAT guidance actually delivered or exceeded. Until then, the stock is range-bound between the restructuring drag and the quality franchise premium.

analysis.summary: COH delivered a significant earnings miss versus its own long-term targets, with underlying NPAT falling 22% to $322m on flat constant-currency revenue, driven by gross margin compression of 3ppts, a 15% R&D cost surge and $69m in transitional costs. The primary culprit is structural: gross margin collapsed from 74% to 71% on adverse sales mix (more low-priced emerging-market units), manufacturing under-absorption and FX headwinds, not one-off noise. Cash quality was a genuine bright spot — operating cash flow surged 55% to $368m driven by working capital unwind post Nexa inventory build, but this is a one-time tailwind, not a recurring earnings proxy. The final dividend was cut 40% to $1.30 vs $2.15, signalling management's candid acknowledgment that the profit base is materially lower and a reset of payout expectations. The single biggest forward risk is that FY27 guidance of $330-350m underlying NPAT implies only modest recovery, and achieving it requires adult referral pathway improvement and Western European stabilisation — both outside Cochlear's direct control.
analysis.full_analysis:
## Executive summary
- **Earnings collapse**: Underlying NPAT fell 22% to $322m, statutory NPAT fell 62% to $147m; the $175m gap to statutory is dominated by $109m non-cash write-down of Epiminder (innovation fund) and $66m cloud computing expense classified as significant items.
- **Gross margin is the core problem**: Margin fell 3ppts to 71%, driven by adverse geographic and product mix (more China low-tier units), manufacturing under-absorption (production cut due to weaker demand), and FX — all structural headwinds, not one-offs.
- **Red flag — R&D creep**: R&D jumped 15% to $323m (14% of sales), while revenue grew only 2% CC. Management is investing through the trough but this is compressing near-term margins materially.
- **Cash was flattered**: OCF of $368m (+55%) was largely a working capital reversal (Nexa pre-build unwind of ~$277m); underlying cash generation is substantially weaker than this headline.
- **FY27 guidance is modest and vague**: $330-350m underlying NPAT implies 2-9% recovery off a low base; low single-digit CC revenue growth is well below the 10% long-term target.

## Key numbers
| Metric | FY26 | FY25 | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sales revenue (reported) | A$2,343.4m | A$2,355.8m | -1% (+2% CC) |
| Sales revenue — CI segment | A$1,435.2m | A$1,470.2m | -2% (flat CC) |
| Sales revenue — Services | A$634.9m | A$609.2m | +4% (+6% CC) |
| Sales revenue — Acoustics | A$273.3m | A$276.4m | -1% (+1% CC) |
| Gross profit | A$1,655.4m | A$1,740.6m | -5% |
| Gross margin | 71% | 74% | -3ppts |
| EBIT (underlying) | A$432.6m | A$554.0m | -22% (-20% CC) |
| EBIT margin (underlying) | 18% | 24% | -6ppts |
| Underlying NPAT | A$322.4m | A$414.5m | -22% |
| Underlying NPAT margin | 14% | 18% | -4ppts |
| Statutory NPAT | A$147.3m | A$388.9m | -62% |
| Underlying vs statutory bridge | -$175.1m after tax: cloud computing -$66m; fair value/impairment (Epiminder) -$109.1m | | |
| Operating cash flow | A$368.0m | A$237.6m | +55% |
| Capital expenditure | A$90.7m | A$102.6m | -12% |
| Free cash flow | A$263.5m | A$122.4m | +115% |
| Net cash | A$187.7m | A$275.7m | -$88.0m |
| R&D expense | A$323.2m | A$281.2m | +15% |
| CI units sold | 56,692 | 53,968 | +5% |

## Quality of earnings
- **Cash conversion optically strong but misleading**: OCF of $368m vs underlying NPAT of $322m looks like 114% cash conversion, but $94.3m of cloud expense flows through OCF (not P&L under underlying), so adjusted OCF is closer to $274m, giving roughly 85% conversion — acceptable but not exceptional.
- **Working capital reversal is non-recurring**: The $277m positive working capital swing reflects unwinding of FY25's Nexa System inventory pre-build. This is not a sustainable annual contribution; FY25's OCF of $238m was suppressed for the same reason. Normalised OCF is somewhere in the $280-320m range.
- **One-offs are chunky and recurring-ish**: The cloud computing charge ($66m after tax in FY26, $22.9m in FY25) is being treated as significant but appears to recur. Management retrospectively reclassified FY25's cloud charge as significant for comparability — a useful disclosure but investors should note this item is not truly non-recurring.
- **Epiminder write-down ($109m after tax)**: This is a genuine non-cash impairment of innovation fund investments. Material but non-cash; reduces net assets but does not affect underlying earnings.
- **Receivables and DSO**: Trade receivables fell from $593.7m to $568.4m, broadly in line with the revenue decline; no obvious receivables quality concern.
- **Inventory**: Fell from $499.4m to $491.3m, consistent with the post-Nexa-launch normalisation narrative.
- **Capitalised costs**: Intangibles fell from $500.8m to $483.2m net — no aggressive capitalisation detected; capex of $90.7m is described as stay-in-business only.

## Management framing
**Rating: Mixed — largely transparent on numbers but promotional on outlook confidence**
- **Transparent**: Management directly stated FY26 was "below expectations" and acknowledged a "decline in shareholder value" — uncommon candour for a blue-chip company. The reconciliation between underlying and statutory profit is clear and the $69m transitional cost breakdown ($32m restructuring + $37m STI provision replenishment) is specific.
- **Promotional / incomplete**: The $37m STI provision replenishment is buried in transitional costs. This is a real cash cost that will recur in a recovery year — it is not truly 'transitional'. Stripping it alongside restructuring is mildly misleading.
- **Downplayed**: The cloud computing expense is large and appears semi-permanent (growing from $32.7m to $94.3m cash in one year), yet it is excluded from underlying profit every year. Investors should treat this as a recurring cost in any normalised earnings assessment.
- **Constant currency used selectively**: Revenue is discussed primarily in CC terms (+2%), masking the -1% reported decline. This is standard but worth noting.
- **Confident language on long-term targets despite missing near-term**: The 10% revenue growth and 18% margin targets remain stated, despite FY26 delivering +2% CC growth and 14% margin. FY27 guidance of $330-350m is well below the implied 18% margin trajectory.

## Segments
| Segment | FY26 Revenue | FY25 Revenue | Change (reported) | Change (CC) | Mix |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cochlear Implants | A$1,435.2m | A$1,470.2m | -2% | flat | 61% |
| Services | A$634.9m | A$609.2m | +4% | +6% | 27% |
| Acoustics | A$273.3m | A$276.4m | -1% | +1% | 12% |
- **CI**: Units +5% but revenue flat CC — average selling price fell, driven by China volume-based procurement (lower ASP) and higher emerging-market mix. Western Europe declined 8% reported. US grew 4% reported.
- **Services**: The standout performer at +6% CC; structural tailwind from growing installed base and Nucleus 8 processor upgrade cycle. Developed market Services +13%.
- **Acoustics**: Flat after a soft first half (competitor pressure in US/UK); H2 +5% CC from Osia expansion into Western Europe and Asia Pacific. No segment EBIT margin disclosed by segment.

## Balance sheet
- **Net cash of $187.7m** (down from $275.7m), still a strong position with no debt concerns flagged.
- **Capital employed fell $121.8m** to $1,552.8m, primarily due to the Epiminder write-down reducing investments.
- **Equity fell $209.8m** to $1,740.5m, primarily reflecting the write-down plus dividends exceeding retained profits.
- **Working capital / revenue** stable at 34%.
- **No refinancing risk** disclosed; the company appears predominantly equity-funded with net cash position.
- **Covenants**: Not mentioned — not a concern given the net cash position.

## Dividend and capital allocation
- **Full year dividend: A$3.45/share** (-20%), comprising interim A$2.15 (flat) + final A$1.30 (-40%).
- **Payout ratio: 70%** of underlying NPAT (vs 68% in FY25) — payout ratio held broadly stable but the base fell sharply.
- **85% franked** (final dividend); strong for Australian investors.
- **Share buyback**: Nil in FY26 vs $28.2m in FY25 — buybacks suspended, appropriate given earnings reset.
- **Capex of $90.7m** described as stay-in-business only; the major innovation pipeline (totally implantable, drug-eluting electrode) is expensed through R&D ($323m), not capitalised.
- **The final dividend cut of 40% is a significant signal**: Management is not defending the payout at the expense of the balance sheet, which is prudent but will disappoint income investors.

## Guidance and outlook
- **FY27 guidance**: Underlying net profit of **A$330-350m** (implying +2% to +9% recovery); low single-digit CC sales revenue growth.
- This is explicit numerical guidance — uncommon for COH to give point guidance — which itself signals management uncertainty about the pace of recovery.
- The A$330-350m midpoint of $340m implies a net margin of approximately 14-15%, well below the 18% long-term target.
- No timeline provided for returning to 10% revenue growth or 18% margin targets.
- Key swing factors cited: adult referral pathway improvement, Western Europe stabilisation, Nexa pricing accretion, and cost restructuring benefits.

## Positives
- **Nexa System launch**: >95% of developed market implant sales by June; 3% average price lift; upgradeable firmware creates recurring software-based value; strong clinician and patient feedback.
- **Services resilience**: +6% CC growth; structurally supported by ~800,000+ recipient installed base; Nucleus 8 upgrade cycle visible.
- **Free cash flow**: $263.5m (+115%) provides genuine financial flexibility despite the earnings decline.
- **Totally implantable pivotal studies commenced ahead of schedule**: Long-dated but this is the product that could materially expand the addressable market.
- **Market share maintained at >60%** globally despite competitive and macro pressures.
- **Management candour**: Explicit acknowledgment of underperformance, restructuring actions, and STI reset; rare for large-cap ASX companies.
- **R&D investment maintained at $323m** (14% of revenue) — protecting long-term competitive position.

## Negatives / red flags
- **Gross margin structural deterioration**: 71% vs 74%; the mix shift to lower-priced emerging market units and China pricing resets from volume-based procurement are not easily reversible. Manufacturing under-absorption could persist if demand remains soft.
- **Cloud computing charge is a recurring hidden cost**: $94.3m cash / $66m after-tax excluded from underlying NPAT in FY26; grew dramatically from FY25. True underlying FCF is materially lower than headline.
- **Epiminder write-down ($109m after tax)**: Innovation fund investments of $52.6m (from $189.4m) are now a much smaller residual; the write-down signals the innovation portfolio strategy had poor capital allocation outcomes.
- **Western Europe structural weakness**: UK surgery backlogs, Spain industrial action, Germany market share loss — multiple country-specific issues occurring simultaneously may indicate a deeper market penetration problem, not purely temporary headwinds.
- **Adult referral pathway dependency**: The core growth thesis relies on making adult cochlear implantation the 'standard of care' — this is a multi-year market development effort with high execution risk and significant dependence on clinician and payer behaviour change outside Cochlear's control.
- **FX headwind**: AUD strengthening reduced underlying NPAT by $24m; hedging smooths but does not eliminate exposure; COH earns predominantly in USD/EUR.
- **STI provision replenishment ($37m)**: Classified as transitional cost in FY26 but is simply the restoration of a normal incentive pool after FY25's below-target payout. This will recur if performance meets targets — not a one-off.
- **FY27 guidance well below long-term targets**: Midpoint $340m implies ~14% NPAT margin vs 18% target; no credible bridge provided to the 18% target.

## Bottom line
**Bull case**: Nexa platform drives sustained ASP uplift and software-enabled margin expansion; adult referral pathway investment (ENT pilots in 12 US cities expanding to Germany/Australia) generates more consistent unit growth; Western Europe headwinds prove transitory; totally implantable cochlear implant reaches market in 3-5 years and opens a new market segment. Services compound at mid-single digits on installed base growth. Operating leverage on any revenue recovery drives margins back toward 18%. At $330-350m NPAT and a ~30x PE, the stock is already pricing in significant recovery.

**Bear case**: Adult referral pathways remain structurally inconsistent; China pricing pressure spreads; gross margin stays below 72% as mix shifts persist; R&D at 14% of sales is non-negotiable given the pipeline; cloud costs continue to grow and remain excluded from underlying profit; FX remains a drag; and FY27 guidance of $330-350m proves optimistic. In this scenario, the 18% margin target is 3+ years away and the stock derate continues.

**What would change the view**: (1) Evidence that US adult referral rates are improving — quantified surgeon referral data from ENT pilot cities; (2) Western Europe returning to growth within two quarters; (3) Gross margin recovery to >72% in H1 FY27; (4) Clarity on whether the cloud computing charge will eventually cease or plateau. Any of these would meaningfully de-risk the recovery thesis.

analysis.summary: Strong beat on all metrics driven by the double NRL and NRLW premiership win, with revenue up 20.5% and NPAT up 36% on pcp. The key drivers were merchandise (+121%), sponsorship (+17%), and a $1.75m one-off ARLC competition expansion payment that will not fully repeat. Operating cash conversion was exceptional at 177% of NPAT, aided by a $5.0m surge in unearned revenue (forward bookings for 2026 season). The ordinary dividend of 2c plus a 1c special reflects confidence but the payout ratio remains conservative at just 38% of NPAT. The single biggest forward risk is revenue mean-reversion: the 2025 result was heavily inflated by once-in-a-generation premiership economics (finals incentives, merchandise uplift, TV bonuses), and sustaining that commercial base without on-field success in 2026 will be extremely difficult.
analysis.full_analysis:
## Executive summary
- **Best result in years:** Revenue $98.3m (+20.5%), NPAT $7.8m (+36%), EBITDA $11.5m (+37%) — all materially ahead of 2024 on the back of the club's first NRL/NRLW double premiership.
- **Premiership economics are real but lumpy:** Merchandise alone surged from $4.4m to $9.7m (+121%); sponsorship +17%; ticketing/game day/membership +12.4%; and the club received $1.75m of a $4m ARLC PNG expansion grant (4 remaining instalments to flow over future years). These are not recurring at the same magnitude.
- **Cash quality is high this period** — operating cash flow of $13.7m significantly exceeded NPAT of $7.8m, though the $5.0m spike in unearned revenue (pre-sold 2026 memberships/corporate packages) is a timing benefit that pulls 2026 revenue forward.
- **Red flag — concentration and dependency:** ARLC grants ($22.2m, 23% of revenue) remain the single largest revenue item and are subject to a licence agreement running to 2034. The top two shareholders (News Corp 68.87%, BGM Projects 22.05%) own 90.92% — the free float is negligible and the share price ($1.45 at year-end) is acknowledged by directors to not reflect underlying value.
- **No forward earnings guidance provided.**

## Key numbers

| Metric | FY25 | FY24 | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Total revenue | $98.3m | $81.6m | +20.5% |
| Operating revenue (ex-interest) | $96.97m | $80.26m | +20.8% |
| ARLC grants | $22.2m | $19.6m | +13.2% |
| Sponsorship | $18.1m | $15.5m | +16.8% |
| Membership/ticketing/game day | $31.3m | $27.8m | +12.4% |
| Merchandise (sale of goods) | $9.7m | $4.4m | +120.7% |
| Total expenses | $87.0m | $73.2m | +18.9% |
| EBITDA (unaudited) | $11.5m | $8.4m | +36.9% |
| EBITDA margin | 11.7% | 10.3% | +140bps |
| Profit before tax | $11.3m | $8.4m | +35.1% |
| Income tax expense | -$3.6m | -$2.7m | +33.5% |
| Statutory NPAT | $7.8m | $5.7m | +35.9% |
| Basic EPS | 7.9c | 5.8c | +36.2% |
| Operating cash flow | $13.7m | $7.1m | +92.0% |
| Free cash flow (OCF less capex) | $11.3m | $5.3m | +112% |
| Cash and equivalents | $36.0m | $26.7m | +34.9% |
| Net cash (debt-free) | $36.0m | $26.7m | +34.9% |
| Net assets | $53.6m | $47.8m | +12.1% |

*No underlying/adjusted number disclosed — statutory figure used throughout.*

## Quality of earnings
- **Cash conversion is outstanding on the surface:** OCF of $13.7m vs NPAT of $7.8m = 177% conversion. However, $5.0m of that is unearned revenue (pre-collected 2026 season revenue) — strip that out and normalised conversion is ~113%, which is still solid.
- **Merchandise revenue quality is real but cyclical:** Cost of sales jumped from $2.8m to $6.2m (+122%), so gross margin on merchandise is thin and volume-driven; a non-premiership year will see this line halve.
- **One-off items in revenue:** (1) $1.75m ARLC PNG expansion payment (first of 5 instalments — remaining $2.25m spread over future years); (2) insurance proceeds recognised in 'other revenue' (jumped from $37k to $1.2m); (3) NRL/NRLW prizemoney surged from $525k to $856k. These three items total approximately $3.1m of non-recurring revenue in FY25.
- **Receivables DSO:** Trade receivables grew from $1.76m to $2.61m (+48%), and $757k is past due (vs $198k in 2024) — worth monitoring but not yet alarming given revenue growth.
- **Capex:** $2.45m in FY25 (vs $1.83m in FY24), modest and well within cash generation. No capital expenditure commitments at 31 December 2025.
- **Off-balance-sheet commitments:** Football/player/community contracts total $47.5m ($24.3m within 1 year, $23.3m 1-5 years) — up from $44.3m. These are the dominant fixed cost obligation and grow with CBA escalation regardless of on-field performance.

## Management framing
**Rating: Promotional — but not misleading.**
- The Chairman and CEO letters are relentlessly positive and premiership-centric, which is understandable but provides zero financial nuance.
- The Directors' Report does explicitly call out the one-off ARLC PNG payment ($1.75m) and the insurance proceeds, which is transparent.
- EBITDA is presented as an 'unaudited non-IFRS measure' with a footnote — appropriate.
- **Downplayed:** The membership count actually *fell* from 61,280 to 60,541 (total members down 1.2%), with non-ticketed memberships down 9%. Management buried this inside the ticketing section and emphasised average crowd growth instead. This is a leading indicator of commercial momentum worth watching.
- **Omitted:** No discussion of what revenue would look like in a non-finals year. No sensitivity analysis. No forward guidance whatsoever.
- The share price re-rating from $0.95 to $1.45 (+53%) is noted but directors explicitly caveat that given 90.9% concentrated ownership and illiquid float, it does not reflect underlying value — this is unusually candid.

## Segments
The Group operates as a **single segment** (NRL/NRLW football team management). No sub-segment disclosure is required or provided. Revenue categories from Note 6:

| Revenue stream | FY25 | FY24 | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Membership/ticketing/corporate/game day | $31.3m | $27.8m | +12.4% |
| Sponsorship | $18.1m | $15.5m | +16.8% |
| Community programs | $10.5m | $9.7m | +8.2% |
| Sale of goods (merchandise) | $9.7m | $4.4m | +120.7% |
| ARLC grants | $22.2m | $19.6m | +13.2% |
| Royalties and commissions | $1.6m | $1.1m | +40.0% |
| Prizemoney/participation/naming rights | $0.9m | $0.5m | +63.1% |
| Interest income | $1.3m | $1.3m | +2.7% |
| Other (incl insurance proceeds) | $1.2m | $0.04m | n/m |

## Balance sheet
- **Debt-free:** No bank debt, no borrowings. Cash of $36.0m (up from $26.7m), comprising $31m in short-term deposits (90-day) and $5m at-call. Earning ~4.5% pa ($1.3m interest income).
- **Net assets $53.6m** (up from $47.8m), including $12.5m sporting franchise intangible (indefinite life, impairment tested annually using 9.3% discount rate, 3% growth — no impairment in FY25).
- **Unearned revenue jumped to $15.0m** (from $10.1m) — a $5.0m increase reflecting early pre-sale of 2026 season memberships and corporate packages. This is a liability but a high-quality one (cash already received).
- **Employee provisions** growing: current $2.7m (up from $2.2m), non-current $0.4m. Salary and wages $37.6m (up 11.9% from $33.6m) — the dominant cost line.
- **Working capital is strong:** Current ratio 2.2x. No covenant risk (no debt).
- **Franking account balance:** $15.3m after proposed dividend — substantial buffer for future fully-franked distributions.

## Dividend and capital allocation
- **FY25 ordinary final dividend:** 2.0 cents per share, 100% franked at 30%, declared 27 February 2026 (not yet in FY25 accounts).
- **Special dividend:** 1.0 cent per share declared alongside — excluded from ordinary dividend. Total FY25 distribution = 3.0c/share = $2.94m total cash outflow.
- **Payout ratio:** 3.0c total / 7.9c EPS = 38% — extremely conservative given $36m cash on balance sheet.
- The prior year paid 2.0c (FY24 final), so ordinary dividend is flat year-on-year despite a 36% earnings increase. The special dividend was the concession to shareholders.
- With $36m cash, $0 debt, and free float of <10%, capital management optionality is limited. A buyback is impractical given illiquidity. The Board could increase the ordinary dividend substantially without straining the balance sheet.

## Guidance and outlook
**No quantitative guidance provided for FY26.** The Directors' Report explicitly states further information on likely developments has been excluded to avoid 'unreasonable prejudice.' The qualitative commentary acknowledges: (1) competition for discretionary consumer spending remains challenging; (2) the NRLW program will continue to evolve; (3) technology and innovation investment will continue. No revenue, earnings, or dividend targets disclosed.

## Positives
- **Double premiership in FY25** drove a multi-year high in revenue, NPAT, and cash generation across all commercial metrics simultaneously.
- **Debt-free balance sheet with $36m cash** (~37c/share) provides significant downside protection and optionality.
- **ARLC funding agreement secured to November 2034** ($22.2m in FY25, growing with contracted increases) provides a stable ~23% revenue floor.
- **Operating cash conversion 177%** — the business collects cash before delivering the service (unearned revenue model is highly capital-efficient).
- **Merchandise business re-rated:** $9.7m in FY25 vs $4.4m shows the potential scale of this revenue line under the right conditions, and management invested in inventory management to support it.
- **ARLC PNG expansion payment:** $2.25m of additional grant payments still to flow over 4 remaining instalments — visible future revenue.
- **Community programs revenue growing** (+8.2%) and government-funded, providing diversification.
- **EPS growth trajectory is compelling** over 5 years: 3.0c (FY21) to 7.9c (FY25), a 163% increase.

## Negatives / red flags
- **Premiership revenue is not repeatable:** An estimated $3-5m of FY25 revenue is directly attributable to one-off premiership economics (finals incentives, merchandise spike, insurance proceeds, first ARLC PNG tranche). A miss on finals in FY26 could compress NPAT by 30-40%.
- **Total membership fell** from 61,280 to 60,541 (-1.2%), with non-ticketed members down 9.3% — a structural softening in the fan base that is directionally concerning.
- **Salary and wage cost inflation is structural:** Player CBA escalation means football operations costs ($27.9m, +10.7%) and total wages ($37.6m, +11.9%) will grow regardless of on-field results.
- **Extreme ownership concentration:** News Corp (68.87%) + BGM Projects (22.05%) = 90.92%. Minority shareholders have no meaningful influence and the stock is effectively untradeable. Directors themselves note the share price does not reflect underlying value.
- **CEO bonus structure is opaque:** Mr Donaghy received $300k bonus in FY25 (vs $100k in FY24, a 200% increase) for 'incentivised metrics and discretionary incentives' — the split between formula-driven and discretionary is not disclosed.
- **The Star Entertainment Group is a premier sponsor and is in significant financial distress** — any collapse of that partnership would impact sponsorship revenue.
- **No guidance, no forward visibility:** Investors are flying blind into FY26 with no quantitative anchor.
- **Free float liquidity is near-zero:** 318 shareholders hold less than a marketable parcel; the stock is essentially a private company that happens to be listed.

## Bottom line
**Bull case:** The Broncos have proven they can generate $7-8m NPAT in a premiership year with a lean, debt-free balance sheet. The ARLC funding agreement to 2034 provides a $22m+ revenue floor. If the team remains competitive in FY26 (finals contender), merchandise, sponsorship, and ticketing can sustain at $70-80% of FY25 levels. The $36m cash pile is worth 37c/share against a $1.45 price, and the franking account is fat. At these settings, the stock trades at ~18x normalised earnings — not cheap, but defensible for a near-monopoly sports franchise.

**Bear case:** FY25 NPAT was inflated by $3-5m of non-recurring items. Strip those out and normalised earnings are closer to $4-5m (5-6c EPS). A non-finals season in FY26 with CBA-driven cost escalation could see NPAT revert to $4-5m, implying the current share price is 29-36x normalised earnings — expensive for an illiquid, News Corp-controlled microcap with no buyback capacity.

**What would change the view:** (1) Sustained finals appearances over 2-3 years demonstrating the commercial base is structurally higher; (2) membership growth resuming above 62,000; (3) any move by News Corp to monetise its stake or take the company private at a control premium; (4) ARLC renegotiating the funding agreement upward; or (5) introduction of a meaningful ongoing dividend policy above 50% payout.
